questions.question: Who is credited with setting up of Brahmo Sabha, for religious reforms, in 1828, which was later called Brahma Samaj?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raja Ram Mohan Roy.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy:-**

 
 
• **He is credited with setting up of Brahmo Sabha in 1828, which later became known as Brahma Samaj.**
 
• He was a social reformer who advocated for the abolition of practices such as Sati and child marriage. 
 
• Roy's efforts towards religious and social reform paved the way for the Indian Renaissance.
 
 
 
• **Brahma Samaj:-**
 
 
• It was founded as a monotheistic Hindu reform movement that emphasized the worship of one God and the rejection of idol worship.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rabindranath Tagore:-**

 
 
• He was a poet, writer, and philosopher who was associated with the Indian independence movement.
 
• While he was a follower of the Brahma Samaj and was influenced by Raja Ram Mohan Roy's ideas, he was not involved in setting up the movement.
 
 
 
• **Keshub Chandra Sen:-**
 
 
• Keshub Chandra Sen was a disciple of Raja Ram Mohan Roy and played a significant role in the development of the Brahma Samaj.
 
• He later broke away from the Brahma Samaj and founded his own movement, the Brahmo Samaj of India.
 
 
 
• **Devendra Nath Tagore:-**
 
 
• Devendra Nath Tagore was a follower of Raja Ram Mohan Roy and played an important role in the development of the Brahma Samaj.
 
• He was the father of Rabindranath Tagore and was a prominent figure in the Bengal Renaissance.

questions.question: Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the _______, an organisation that attempted to reform Hinduism.
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Swami Dayanand Saraswati:-****​**

 
 
• Dayananda Saraswati [1824-1883] was the first to give the call for Swarajya – "India for Indians" – in 1876.
 
• For his own inspiration, Swami Dayanand went to the Vedas which he regarded as infallible.
 
• He rejected all later religious thought if it conflicted with the Vedas.
 
• This total dependence on Vedas and their infallibility gave his teachings orthodox coloring.
 
• He was opposed to idolatry, ritual, and priesthood and particularly to the prevalent caste practices and popular Hinduism as preached by Brahmins
 
• ​Swami Dayanand met Keshub Chandra Sen, Vidyasagar, Justice Ranade, Gopal Hari Deshmukh, and other modern religious and social reformers.
 
• He took inspiration from the Vedas and considered them to be ‘India’s Rock of Ages, the infallible, and the true original seed of Hinduism.
 
• He gave the slogan “Back to the Vedas”.
 
• Dayananda’s slogan of ‘Back to the Vedas’ was a call for a revival of Vedic learning and Vedic purity of religion and not a revival of Vedic times.
 
• He accepted modernity and displayed a patriotic attitude to national problems.
 
 
 
• **Arya Samaj:-**
 
 
• Arya Samaj is a Hindu reform movement founded by 'Swami Dayanand Saraswati'.
 
• Dayanand Saraswati had inspired the Arya Samaj from Swami Virjanand of Mathura in Bombay in 1875.
 
• Arya Samaji believed in pure Vedic tradition and rejected idol worship, avatars, sacrifice, false rituals, and superstitions.
 
• In this, untouchability and caste discrimination were opposed and women and Shudras were also given the right to wear Yagyopaveet and read the Vedas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Vedant Samaj:-**

 
 
• It also known as the Vedanta Society, is a religious and philosophical organization based on the teachings of Vedanta, a school of Hindu philosophy.
 
• Vedanta is derived from the Upanishads, ancient texts that form the philosophical and spiritual foundation of Hinduism.
 
 
 
• **Adi Dharma Samaj:-**
 
 
• It is a religious and social organization based in Bali, Indonesia. It was founded in the early 20th century as a response to the dominant religious practices of the time, which were primarily based on Hinduism.
 
• Adi Dharma Samaj sought to promote a form of Hinduism that was more inclusive and accessible to the local Balinese people.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the 'Satyashodhak Samaj' in 1873?
questions.solution:

__
 
• Jyotiba Phule founded the 'Satyashodhak Samaj' in 1873 in Maharashtra.
 
• The organization aimed to eliminate social discrimination and promote equal rights for lower castes.
 
• Satyashodhak Samaj translates to "Society of Truth Seekers."
 
• Phule's initiative was pivotal in advocating for education and social reforms, especially for women and lower castes.
 
• The movement emphasized rational thinking and opposed the caste system and religious orthodoxy.

• Born on April 11, 1827, in Maharashtra, Jyotiba Phule was a prominent social reformer, thinker, and writer.
 
• He and his wife Savitribai Phule started the first school for girls in Pune in 1848.
 
• Phule wrote several books, including "Gulamgiri" (Slavery), highlighting the plight of lower castes and advocating for their rights.
 
• He is often referred to as the 'Father of Indian Social Revolution' for his efforts in fighting caste discrimination and promoting education.
 
 
 
• **Satyashodhak Samaj's Impact**
 
 
• The organization played a crucial role in the social awakening of lower castes in Maharashtra and other parts of India.
 
• It laid the foundation for subsequent social reform movements and the rise of Dalit activism in India.
 
• The principles of Satyashodhak Samaj inspired many future leaders, including Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
 
 
 
• **Social Reforms of the 19th Century**
 
 
• The 19th century in India saw a wave of social reform movements aimed at eradicating social evils like caste discrimination, child marriage, and sati.
 
• Other notable reformers of the era include Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, and Swami Dayananda Saraswati.
 
 
 
• **Education and Social Change**
 
 
• Education was seen as a powerful tool for social change and empowerment during the 19th century.
 
• Reformers like Phule emphasized the need for educating women and lower castes to break the cycle of oppression and poverty.

questions.question: Who among the following was the pioneer of 'Bhoodan Movement'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Acharya Vinoba Bhave**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Acharya Vinoba Bhave** was the pioneer of the **Bhoodan Movement**, which aimed at redistributing land to landless farmers.
 
• The movement began in **1951** at Pochampally village in Telangana, where Vinoba Bhave persuaded wealthy landowners to donate land for the poor.
 
• The term "Bhoodan" translates to "**Land Donation**" and was a non-violent initiative inspired by Gandhian philosophy.
 
• Vinoba Bhave walked across villages, requesting landowners to donate a part of their land voluntarily to the landless, promoting **social equality**.
 
• By 1954, the movement expanded into the **Gramdan Movement**, where entire villages donated land for community welfare.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vinoba Bhave** was a spiritual leader and a prominent disciple of Mahatma Gandhi, deeply committed to the principles of non-violence and selfless service.
 
• The **Bhoodan Movement** was a part of larger Gandhian efforts to address rural poverty and land inequality in post-independence India.
 
• The movement significantly influenced the concept of **land reforms** in India, although its success varied across regions.
 
• The **Gramdan Movement**, derived from Bhoodan, aimed to promote collective ownership of land and community-driven development.
 
• Vinoba Bhave received the **Ramon Magsaysay Award** for his social and leadership efforts in 1958.

questions.question: Who was the social reformer and political leader who championed women's rights and played a significant role in the Widow Remarriage Act of 1856?

__
 
• Ishwarchandra Vidyasagar

 
 
• Ishwarchandra Vidyasagar, a Bengali reformer, actively raised the issues related to women.
 
• He was an active proponent of the education of girl children as he believed that lack of education was the real cause underlying all their problems.
 
• With the help of an Englishman named Bethune, he set up many schools devoted especially to girl children.

• Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a person of wide knowledge or learning from Bengal India and a key figure of the Bengal Renaissance.
 
• He was an academic educator, philosopher, publisher, entrepreneur, philanthropist, writer, translator, printer, and reformer.
 
• He simplified and modernized Bengali prose. Hence considered the "Father of Bengali prose". 
 
• Also rationalized and simplified the Bengali alphabet and type, which had remained unchanged since Charles Wilkins and Panchanan Karmakar had cut the first (wooden) Bengali type in 1780.
 
• His graduation college, Sanskrit College, Calcutta gave him the title “Vidyasagar”, due to his excellent performance in Sanskrit studies and philosophy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• He attended the parliament of religions held in Chicago on 11th September 1893.

• **Dayananda Saraswati**

 
 
• Born on 12th February 1824, Dayananda Saraswati was a significant Indian thinker, social reformer, and founder of the Arya Samaj movement, which aimed at reforming Vedic dharma.
 
• He was also known as Mulshankar.
 
• In 1876, he was a pioneer in advocating for Swaraj (self-rule), promoting the idea that India should be governed by Indians, a sentiment that would later be echoed by other leaders like Lokmanya Tilak.
 
• Dayananda Saraswati emphasized the principles of Karma (action) and Reincarnation (the cycle of birth and rebirth) in his teachings.
 
• He was also a proponent of equal rights for women, working towards their upliftment and advocating for their education and equal status in society.
 
• In 1883, Maharaja Jaswant Singh II of Jodhpur invited him to the palace, expressing a desire to become his disciple and learn from his teachings.
 
• Dayananda Saraswati demonstrated his scholarly prowess in a debate held in Varanasi in 1869, where he emerged victorious against a gathering of 27 scholars and 12 expert pandits, with an audience of over 50,000 people.
 
• Throughout his lifetime, he authored more than 60 works, including a significant 16-volume explanation of the six Vedangas, which are auxiliary disciplines associated with the study and understanding of the Vedas.
 
• He also began but did not complete a commentary on the Ashtadhyayi, an ancient Sanskrit treatise on grammar written by Panini, showcasing his deep engagement with classical Sanskrit texts and his scholarly contributions to understanding and interpreting them.

• In 1925, Bhagat Singh returned to Lahore and within the next year he and his colleagues started a militant youth organisation called the Naujawan Bharat Sabha.
 
• In 1928, he was associated with the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) along with Sukhdev, Chandrashekhar Azad and others.
 
• Bhagat Singh and Sukhdev also organized the Lahore Students Union for open, legal work among the students.
 
 
 
• Revolutionary activities he was involved in:

• 1929 Central Assembly Bombing Case.

• The trio was ordered to be hanged on 24 March 1931 but the sentence was carried out a day earlier at the Lahore Jail.

__
 
• **Bharat Sevak Samaj or ****The Servants of India Society** was formed in Pune, Maharashtra, on June 12, 1905 by **Gopal Krishna Gokhale.**
 
• **The purpose of samaj was to find and develop avenues of voluntary service for the citizens of India. To promote national sufficiency and to build up the economic strength of the country.**
 
• The aim of 'The Servants of Indian Society' was to train national missionaries for service to India and promote the true interests of the Indian people by constitutional means alone.
 
• Gopal Krishna Gokhale was called the **'Diamond of India'** by his political opponent Bal Gangadhar Tilak. Gopal Krishna Gokhale was an Indian liberal political leader and a social reformer.

questions.question: Which one of the following does 'Nirguna Bhakti' refer to?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__**:Abstract form of God worship**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **Nirguna Bhakt**i is an** abstract form of God worship that is prevalent in Hinduism.**
 
• The term **"Nirguna" refers to the concept of God being formless, attributeless,** and beyond the material world.
 
• In Nirguna Bhakti, **the focus is on worshipping the formless aspect of God, rather than a specific deity with attributes and characteristics.**
 
• The **practice of Nirguna Bhakti involves meditating on the divine and surrendering oneself to the ultimate reality**, which is considered to be **beyond human comprehension**.
 
• The** aim **of this form of worship is to **transcend the limitations of the material world and achieve a state of oneness with the divine**.
 
• Nirguna Bhakti is often associated with the teachings of the great Hindu** saints and mystics**, such as **Kabir, Namdev, and Ravidas,**
 
• who **rejected the traditional forms of deity worship and emphasized the importance of devotion to the formless divine.**
 
• These **saints believed that true devotion could only be achieved through the practice of inner meditation and contemplation, rather than external rituals and offerings.**
